Reader-funded newsletter by Keyana Sapp, published on beehiiv (rss.beehiiv.com/feeds/J17ICFTI1f.xml), investigating how trusted consumer brands got cheaper to make and quicker to break, and who profited from the decline.
No ads, affiliate links, or sponsors; funded by reader memberships/donations.
Each edition takes one product category and traces the ownership chain behind the decline:
Cookware — Pyrex, Corelle, Instant Pot, and Oneida consolidated under one buyout firm.

Running shoes — most brands abandoned factory ownership for a shared pool of contract manufacturers.

Maintains a companion "Brand Ledger" database rating brand ownership history and current purchase-worthiness.

Enshittification names a decline specific to digital platforms: subsidize users, shift value to business customers, then extract from everyone — enabled by lock-in, switching costs, and network effects.

Worse on Purpose documents a parallel decline in physical goods, but the mechanism differs: private-equity and conglomerate rollups acquire trusted brand names, consolidate manufacturing onto the same small pool of contract factories, and cut material and build quality while holding the brand and price steady — extracting against accumulated reputation rather than platform lock-in.

The two converge on the same effect: competition that looks real on the surface (different platforms, different brands) turns out to run on the same underlying extraction, and "switching" stops being a real exit — to a different app owned by the same conglomerate, or a different label off the same factory line.

When I was younger, at any one time I had only a single journal. Entries were sequential. Over time, the volumes of handwritten pages became the way I picture the passage of time. When I look upon my old journals, each volume appears as an epoch, a geological strata in the development of my life. The journals became Horcrux into which I pasted concert tickets, pressed leaves,
, a geological strata representing a period of. I didn't scrapbook as much as people in my family circle did, but I did sketch and paste physical artifacts into my journals.
